title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The image is extremely faint. It looks like an erased draft, or a show-through, of the next page (153), and the legible fragments match that page almost line for line. The setting is as follows.

- K is a Galois CM field over Q with group G. Complex conjugation ρ generates γ = {1,ρ}, which is central in G.
- M is the G-module of functions φ: G → Z with φ(ρσ) = −φ(σ), so M ≅ Z' ⊗_{Z[γ]} Z[G] = Ind_γ^G Z'. Here Z' is the sign character of γ.
- By descent and duality, M defines a Q-torus T. Up to the duality noted in the margin (M ≅ M̌), T is R_{K^+/Q}(R^1_{K/K^+} G_m), the Weil restriction of the norm-one torus of K/K^+.

Goal (1): compute H^1(Q,T)', the classes in H^1(Q,T) that vanish at every finite place. This is a Tate–Shafarevich-type group that ignores the archimedean places.

The tool is a Tate–Nakayama type exact sequence
0 → H^1(Q,T)' → Ĥ_0(G, Y_∞ ⊗ M̌) → Ĥ_0(G, M̌) → 0,
where Y_∞ is the free group on the infinite places of K and the second map comes from the augmentation Y_∞ → Z.

By Shapiro's lemma, and because ρ fixes every infinite place, this reduces to
0 → H^1' → Y_∞ ⊗ Z/2 → Z/2 → 0.
Hence H^1(Q,T)' is the F_2-space of formal combinations of the infinite places of K with coefficient sum zero. Its dimension is [K:Q]/2 − 1.

Elementary check:
- Shapiro gives H^1(Q,T) = H^1(K^+, K^1) = K^{+*}/N(K^*).
- By the Hasse norm theorem (K/K^+ is cyclic), a class is trivial iff it is a local norm everywhere.
- A class that is trivial at all finite places is therefore detected by signs at the real places of K^+, which are in bijection with the infinite places of K.
- Hilbert reciprocity forces the coefficient sum to be zero, and weak approximation gives surjectivity.

Context: the preceding pages study the Serre group S_K^0 and homomorphisms ψ_Σ: S_K^0 → T_E. This computation of a Hasse-principle defect for a CM-type torus belongs to the same 'Galois theory of motives' (CM motives, Serre/Taniyama group) programme.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the result agrees with the Hasse norm theorem plus Hilbert reciprocity.
The notation is loose: Ĥ_0(γ, Y_∞) on the next page should read Ĥ_0(γ, Y_∞ ⊗ Z'). This is harmless because ρ acts trivially on Y_∞.
This page itself is essentially illegible (a ghost or erased draft of p.153), so any reading of it is conjectural.

ideas.what: Character module M = {φ: G→Z, φ(ρσ) = −φ(σ)} ≅ Ind_γ^G Z' defining the torus R_{K^+/Q}(R^1_{K/K^+} G_m) attached to a Galois CM field
ideas.modern_name: Norm-one torus / CM torus (closely related to the character groups of the Serre group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Ono, Serre; Shimura–Taniyama for the CM context)

ideas.what: Computation of the classes in H^1(Q,T) trivial at all finite places via a Tate–Nakayama exact sequence with Y_∞; answer: sum-zero F_2-combinations of the infinite places
ideas.modern_name: Tate–Nakayama duality / Ш^1 with archimedean places removed; Hasse norm theorem plus Hilbert reciprocity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1966 'The cohomology groups of tori in finite Galois extensions'), Hasse; Kottwitz-style computations later

missed.claim: Within notes on the Galois theory of motives (1965), Grothendieck computes failures of the 'finite-places-only' Hasse principle for CM-type tori. This is the kind of input later used by Langlands, Deligne and Milne–Shih in constructing the Taniyama group and in its uniqueness results, which rest on H^1(Q,S) and local triviality. The page is only a faint draft of p.153, and the computation itself is standard.
missed.quote: On veut calculer le sous-groupe H^1(Q,T)' de H^1(Q,T) formé des classes qui sont nulles en toute place finie
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical evidence that Grothendieck was already probing Galois-cohomological obstructions for motivic tori of CM type in 1965, more than a decade before the Taniyama group (1979–82).

transcription_corrections: The page is a faint erased draft or show-through of p.153. Legible line 1: 'K corps CM [galoisien] sur Q, groupe de Galois G, γ = {1,ρ} ≃ Z/2Z ⊂ G, ρ la conj. complexe'.
Line 2: 'Q̄ une clôture algébrique de Q [contenant] K'.
The boxed passage reads: '[I ensemble des plongements de K dans Q̄] G y opère par transport de structure ... de façon simplement transitive' (crossed out).
Next legible line: 'M groupe des fonctions φ: G → Z telles que φ(ρσ) = −φ(σ) pour tout σ ∈ G'.
Then: 'C'est un G-module, qui définit par descente et dualité un tore T sur Q'.
The margin note reads 'NB M ≃ M̌'.
'(1) On veut calculer le sous-groupe H^1(Q,T)' de H^1(Q,T) formé des classes qui sont nulles en toute place finie'.
The displayed sequence is '0 → Ĥ^1(Q,T)' → Ĥ_0(G, Y_∞ ⊗_Z M̌) → Ĥ_0(G, M̌) → 0'.
Further lines: 'M ≃ Z' ⊗_γ G'; '0 → H^1(Q,T)' → Ĥ_0(γ, Y_∞) → Ĥ_0(γ, Z') → 0'; 'H^1(Q,T)' ≃ groupe des combinaisons linéaires ... des places à l'infini de K, à somme des coefficients nulle'.
